elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 lead-in covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees (Sanofi and its Affiliates).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "an allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, any materials or deliverables provided by RevMed, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party" — the licence-agreement analogue of Services/Deliverables, keyed to the defined term at Section 1.99.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term at Section 1.8; it is not limited by the "in all material respects" qualifier in Section 13.4(b).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data caused by RevMed" — covers all Sanofi data, not merely named categories.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained limb (a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is express.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(a): "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses ..."; unchanged and applies to Section 14.1 as amended.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ..." including appointment of lead counsel.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(e) Cooperation: the Indemnified Party "will cooperate in the defense thereof" and furnish records, witnesses etc. "as may be reasonably requested".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 as amended contains only "(a) any content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with former limbs (b) negligence, (c) warranty breach and (d) material breach struck and (c)/(d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]"; the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization limb is removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.1(d) supplies the Third Party IP infringement/misappropriation limb.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification carve-out is added, which is more favourable to Customer; the stated condition does not apply, so the element is not defeated.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out added; a Customer-favourable absence does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specifications carve-out added; absence is Customer-favourable and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder appears anywhere in the rendered Article XIV; the drafter deliberately took the preferred route instead.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic is inserted; there is no fee-refund language tied to unavailable IP remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fees super-cap is added; Section 14.5 leaves indemnities uncapped (which is better for Customer, and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure).

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Duplicate-direction check: Section 14.1 retains "indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates", so the defence obligation supporting the fallback IP indemnity also exists.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete on the operative text: new Section 14.1(d)–(f) add the IP infringement, Sanofi-data-breach and breach-of-Applicable-Law limbs; retained (a) supplies gross negligence/wilful misconduct; retained Section 14.3(a),(b),(e) supply notice, control of defence and reasonable cooperation; and Section 14.2 is narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.

The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" reflects the pre-redline document and correctly supports the deviation classification (original Section 14.1 had no IP limb while Section 13.5 disclaims non-infringement); inspected in substance, the rendered redline does contain an express IP limb, so that gate is not evidence of a defect in the proposal.

Fallback is not satisfied (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete; the decision to decline a super-cap is Customer-favourable given Section 14.5 leaves indemnities uncapped.

Minimality holds: the insertions are confined to the three missing indemnity limbs, the conforming lead-in change from "(a) through (c)" to "(a) through (f)", and the narrowing of Section 14.2 required by the tenth preferred element; no survival tails, expense allocations, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and existing favourable language (defend obligation, Affiliate coverage, notice/control/cooperation, the Section 14.1 exception carve-outs) is retained.

Intent is preserved: Article XIV cross-references in Sections 14.3, 14.5 and the termination clause remain operative, the [Intentionally omitted.] placeholders avoid renumbering, and no defined term is left dangling (limb (d) uses the defined "RevMed Licensed Technology", Section 1.99).

Watch-point (not a failure): the phrase "or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement" in limb (d) is broader than a bare Services/Deliverables formulation; it is the appropriate licence-deal analogue but expect Vendor pushback and be prepared to fall back to the technology/materials/deliverables wording alone.

Watch-point (not a failure): striking former Section 14.2(a) (Sanofi's Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization) removes the risk allocation that the termination provision at p0522 assumes may exist ("except to the extent Sanofi has an obligation of indemnification under Article XIV"). The carve-out is narrowed rather than broken, but confirm consistency with the Profit/Loss Share Agreement before sending.
